**DynaLM 0.3.2.** A performance patch for ARM CPUs: models that use Q5_0 or Q5_1 weights decode faster. Outputs are bit-identical to 0.3.1.

## Faster

- **Q5_0 and Q5_1 weights on ARM.** The CPU matmul kernels now unpack these formats with NEON, for both decode and prompt processing; before, they used the scalar path. llama.cpp's Q4_K_M files use Q5_0 for tensors whose row length is not a multiple of 256, so this affects common small models such as Qwen2.5-0.5B, SmolLM2-360M and Gemma-3-1B. These were among the models where DynaLM was slower than llama.cpp in the CPU model sweep.
- **Measured on an Apple M4 Pro**, Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M, 8 threads, back to back against the previous engine: **66 to 107 output tokens/s**; median token gap 13.5 to 7.0 ms. Measured on battery in Low Power Mode, so this is an A/B ratio, not an absolute speed. Other models and CPUs have not been measured yet.

## Verified

- `test_qmm`, all formats and kernel tiers against the scalar reference: 974,781 checks passed.
- Qwen2.5-0.5B wikitext-2 perplexity unchanged at 17.6610.
- CI: all 21 jobs passed (Linux, macOS, Windows, sanitizers, GPU backends, packages, Docker).

## Supported environment

As in 0.3.1: macOS on Apple Silicon is verified (one Apple M4 Pro); the Linux, Windows and macOS Intel builds are CI-tested (built and tested in CI without real models). Vulkan and CUDA are experimental. The fast CPU path needs SME (Apple M4 class); other CPUs run ggml's CPU kernels by default.

## Upgrade

Replace the binary, or run the install script again. No settings, files or APIs changed.
